newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israel wants to control Mideast - Syria's Khaddam.
newsitem.headline: Israel wants to control Mideast - Syria's Khaddam.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam was quoted on Thursday as saying that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wanted to control the Middle East militarily and his cabinet would not produce a peace policy.

"Netanyahu's strategy is Israeli military hegemony over the region. He wants Zionism to control the region's geography. So if Netanyahu torpedoes the peace process, he would consider himself to have served his strategy," Khaddam told the London-based Lebanese weekly al-Hawadeth.

"Netanyahu's government includes the most extremist parties in Israel, meaning the Likud in addition to the religious extremists ... Therefore the current Israeli government will not produce a peace policy," he added.

Khaddam reiterated Syria's demands for a full Israeli withdrawal from the Golan Heights as the price for peace with the Jewish state. Netanyahu, who ousted Shimon Peres in May, has rejected these Syrian demands.
Nearly five years of peace talks between Israel and Syria are stalled over the issue of an Israeli troop withdrawal from the strategic plateau it captured from Syria in the 1967 war.

Asked about the possibility of a new military conflict with Israel, Khaddam said: "This matter cannot be discussed this simply. War has its complications and its destructive results. The Israelis know the dangers of war and we don't want war."
He added: "The Arabs' policy is a defensive policy while the Israeli policy is an aggressive, attacking policy."
